verses.en: The same thing happened in Iconium when Paul and Barnabas went into the Jewish synagogue and spoke in such a way that a large group of both Jews and Greeks believed.
verses.ja: イコニオンでも同じことが起こった。パウロとバルナバがユダヤ人の会堂に入って語ったところ、ユダヤ人もギリシア人も非常に多くの人が信仰に入ったのである。

verses.en: But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.
verses.ja: しかし、従おうとしないユダヤ人たちは異邦人を扇動し、兄弟たちに対して悪意を抱かせて心を濁らせた。

verses.en: So they stayed there for a considerable time, speaking out courageously for the Lord, who testified to the message of his grace, granting miraculous signs and wonders to be performed through their hands.
verses.ja: それゆえ、ふたりはそこにかなりの長期間とどまり、主のために大胆に語った。主はその恵みの言葉に証しを立て、彼らの手を通してしるしや奇蹟を行わせてくださったのである。

verses.en: But the population of the city was divided; some sided with the Jews, and some with the apostles.
verses.ja: だが、都の民衆は二分され、ユダヤ人につく者もいれば、使徒たちにつく者もいた。

verses.en: When both the Gentiles and the Jews (together with their rulers) made an attempt to mistreat them and stone them,
verses.ja: 異邦人とユダヤ人が、役人たちと共に、彼らを侮辱し、石で打ち殺そうと企てたとき、

verses.en: Paul and Barnabas learned about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and the surrounding region.
verses.ja: パウロとバルナバはそのことを知って、リカオニアの町々であるリストラとデルベ、およびその周辺地域へ逃れていった。

verses.en: There they continued to proclaim the good news.
verses.ja: そして、その場所でも福音を宣べ伝え続けた。

verses.en: In Lystra sat a man who could not use his feet, lame from birth, who had never walked.
verses.ja: リストラに、足がきかず、生まれつきの足なえで、一度も歩いたことのない男が座っていた。

verses.en: This man was listening to Paul as he was speaking. When Paul stared intently at him and saw he had faith to be healed,
verses.ja: この男がパウロの話を聞いていた。パウロが彼をじっと見つめ、癒やされる信仰があるのを見て、

verses.en: he said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet.” And the man leaped up and began walking.
verses.ja: 大声で言った。「まっすぐ自分の足で立ちなさい。」すると、男は飛び上がって歩き出した。

verses.en: So when the crowds saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, “The gods have come down to us in human form!”
verses.ja: 群衆はパウロがしたことを見て、リカオニアの言葉で叫んだ。「神々が人間の姿になって、私たちのところ手にお下りになったのだ！」

verses.en: They began to call Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.
verses.ja: そしてバルナバをゼウスと呼び、パウロをヘルメスと呼んだ。パウロが主な話し手だったからである。

verses.en: The priest of the temple of Zeus, located just outside the city, brought bulls and garlands to the city gates; he and the crowds wanted to offer sacrifices to them.
verses.ja: 都のすぐ外にあったゼウスの神殿の祭司が、雄牛と花輪を町の門のところに持って来，群衆と共に彼らにいけにえをささげようとした。

verses.en: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard about it, they tore their clothes and rushed out into the crowd, shouting,
verses.ja: しかし、使徒であるバルナバとパウロはこのことを聞くと、自分たちの服を引き裂き、叫びながら群衆の中へと駆け出した。

verses.en: “Men, why are you doing these things? We too are men, with human natures just like you! We are proclaiming the good news to you, so that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made the heaven, the earth, the sea, and everything that is in them.
verses.ja: 「皆さん、なぜこんなことをするのですか。私たちもあなたたちと同じ人間であり、同じような性質を持った者にすぎません。私たちは、あなたたちがこうした空しいものから離れ、天と地と海、そしてその中にあるすべてのものを造られた生ける神に立ち返るようにと、福音を伝えているのです。

verses.en: In past generations he allowed all the nations to go their own ways,
verses.ja: 過ぎ去った時代には、神はすべての国々がそれぞれの道を歩むのを放任しておかれたが、

verses.en: yet he did not leave himself without a witness by doing good, by giving you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, satisfying you with food and your hearts with joy.”
verses.ja: それでも、善を行ってご自身を証ししないでおかれたわけではない。すなわち、天から雨を降らせ、実りの季節を与え、食物をもってあなたたちの心を喜びで満たし、満ち足りさせてくださったのである。」

verses.en: Even by saying these things, they scarcely persuaded the crowds not to offer sacrifice to them.
verses.ja: 彼らはこのように言ったにもかかわらず、群衆が自分たちにいけにえをささげるのをやっとのことで思いとどまらせた。

verses.en: But Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, and after winning the crowds over, they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, presuming him to be dead.
verses.ja: ところが、アンティオキアとイコニオンからユダヤ人たちがやって来て、群衆を味方に引き入れ、パウロを石で打ち、死んだものと思い込んで町の外へ引きずり出した。

verses.en: But after the disciples had surrounded him, he got up and went back into the city. On the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
verses.ja: しかし、弟子たちが彼の周りに集まったとき、彼は起き上がり、町へ戻っていった。そして翌日、バルナバと共にデルベへ出発した。

verses.en: After they had proclaimed the good news in that city and made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, to Iconium, and to Antioch.
verses.ja: ふたりはその町で福音を宣べ伝え、多くの人を弟子にしてから、リストラ、イコニオン、アンティオキアへと引き返した。

verses.en: They strengthened the souls of the disciples and encouraged them to continue in the faith, saying, “We must enter the kingdom of God through many persecutions.”
verses.ja: 彼らは弟子たちの魂を力づけ、「私たちが神の国に入るには、多くの苦難を経なければならない」と言って、信仰にとどまるように勧めた。

verses.en: When they had appointed elders for them in the various churches, with prayer and fasting they entrusted them to the protection of the Lord in whom they had believed.
verses.ja: また、それぞれの教会ごとに長老たちを選任し、祈りと断食をもって、彼らが信じている主にお委ねした。

verses.en: Then they passed through Pisidia and came into Pamphylia,
verses.ja: それから、ピシディアを通り抜けてパンフィリアへ下り、

verses.en: and when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
verses.ja: ペルガで御言葉を語ってから、アタリアへ下った。

verses.en: From there they sailed back to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had now completed.
verses.ja: そこから船でアンティオキアへ戻った。そこは、ふたりが現在成し遂げた働きのために、神の恵みにゆだねられて送り出された場所であった。

verses.en: When they arrived and gathered the church together, they reported all the things God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith for the Gentiles.
verses.ja: 到着すると、彼らは教会の人々を集め、神が自分たちと共にいて行われたすべてのことと、異邦人のために信仰の扉を開いてくださったことを報告した。

verses.en: So they spent considerable time with the disciples.
verses.ja: そして、弟子たちと共にかなりの長期間を過ごした。

1.en: [解説]  Iconium. See the note in 13:51.
[翻訳注]  Grk “they”; the referents (Paul and Barnabas) have been specified in the translation for clarity.
[解説]  See the note on synagogue in 6:9.

2.en: [翻訳注]  Or “embittered their minds” (Grk “their souls”). BDAG 502 s.v. κακόω 2 has “make angry, embitter τὰς ψυχάς τινων κατά τινος poison the minds of some persons against another Ac 14:2.”

3.en: [翻訳注]  The word “there” is not in the Greek text, but is implied.
[解説]  The Lord testified to the message by granting the signs described in the following clause.
[翻訳注]  Here the context indicates the miraculous nature of the signs mentioned.

4.en: [翻訳注]  BDAG 825 s.v. πλῆθος 2.b.γ has this translation for πλῆθος (plhqo").
[翻訳注]  These clauses are a good example of the contrastive μὲν…δέ (men…de) construction: Some “on the one hand” sided with the Jews, but some “on the other hand” sided with the apostles.

5.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “So there came about an attempt” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
[翻訳注]  On this verb see BDAG 1022 s.v. ὑβρίζω.
[翻訳注]  The direct object “them” is repeated after both verbs in the translation for stylistic reasons, although it occurs only after λιθοβολῆσαι (liqobolhsai) in the Greek text.

6.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “they”; the referents (Paul and Barnabas) have been specified in the translation for clarity.

[翻訳注]  Grk “learning about it, fled.” The participle συνιδόντες (sunidonte") has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style. It could also be taken temporally (“when they learned about it”) as long as opening clause of v. 5 is not translated as a temporal clause too, which results in a redundancy.

[解説]  Lystra was a city in Lycaonia about 18 mi (30 km) south of Iconium, a Roman colony that was not on the main roads of Lycaonia. Because of its relative isolation, its local character was able to be preserved.[地図]  For location see JP1-E2; JP2-E2; JP3-E2.
[解説]  Derbe was a city in Lycaonia about 35 mi (60 km) southeast of Lystra.[地図]  For location see JP1-E2; JP2-E2; JP3-E2.

7.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “region, and there.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, καί (kai) has not been translated and a new sentence begun in the translation.
[翻訳注]  The periphrastic construction εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ἦσαν (euangelizomenoi hsan) has been translated as a progressive imperfect.

8.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “And in.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
[解説]  Lystra was a city in Lycaonia about 18 mi (30 km) south of Iconium.[地図]  For location see JP1-E2; JP2-E2; JP3-E2.
[翻訳注]  Grk “powerless in his feet,” meaning he was unable to use his feet to walk.

[翻訳注]  Grk “lame from his mother’s womb” (an idiom).[解説]  The description lame from birth makes clear how serious the condition was, and how real it was. This event is very similar to Acts 3:1-10, except here the lame man’s faith is clear from the start.

9.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “speaking, who.” The relative pronoun has been replaced by the noun “Paul,” and a new sentence begun in the translation because an English relative clause would be very awkward here.

10.en: [翻訳注]  BDAG 722 s.v. ὀρθός 1.a has “stand upright on your feet.”
[翻訳注]  Grk “he”; the referent (the man) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
[翻訳注]  This verb is imperfect tense in contrast to the previous verb, which is aorist. It has been translated ingressively, since the start of a sequence is in view here.

11.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “they lifted up their voice” (an idiom).
[翻訳注]  Grk “in Lycaonian, saying.” The word “language” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is redundant in English and has not been translated.

[翻訳注]  So BDAG 707 s.v. ὁμοιόω 1. However, L&N 64.4 takes the participle ὁμοιωθέντες (Jomoiwqente") as an adjectival participle modifying θεοί (qeoi): “the gods resembling men have come down to us.”[解説]  The gods have come down to us in human form. Greek culture spoke of “divine men.” In this region there was a story of Zeus and Hermes visiting the area (Ovid, Metamorphoses 8.611-725). The locals failed to acknowledge them, so judgment followed. The present crowd was determined not to make the mistake a second time.

12.en: [翻訳注]  The imperfect verb ἐκάλουν (ekaloun) has been translated as an ingressive imperfect.
[解説]  Zeus was the chief Greek deity, worshiped throughout the Greco-Roman world (known to the Romans as Jupiter).
[解説]  Hermes was a Greek god who (according to Greek mythology) was the messenger of the gods and the god of oratory (equivalent to the Roman god Mercury).

13.en: [翻訳注]  The words “the temple of” are not in the Greek text, but are implied. The translation “the priest of (the temple/shrine of) Zeus located before the city” is given for this phrase by BDAG 426 s.v. Ζεύς.
[解説]  See the note on Zeus in the previous verse.

[翻訳注]  Or “wreaths.”[解説]  Garlands were commonly wreaths of wool with leaves and flowers woven in, worn on a person’s head or woven around a staff. They were an important part of many rituals used to worship pagan gods. Although it was an erroneous reaction, the priest’s reaction shows how all acknowledged their power and access to God.
[翻訳注]  The words “to them” are not in the Greek text, but are clearly implied by the response of Paul and Barnabas in the following verse.

14.en: [解説]  The apostles Barnabas and Paul. This is one of only two places where Luke calls Paul an apostle, and the description here is shared with Barnabas. This is a nontechnical use here, referring to a commissioned messenger.
[翻訳注]  The participle ἀκούσαντες (akousante") is taken temporally.

[翻訳注]  Grk “tearing their clothes they rushed out.” The participle διαρρήξαντες (diarrhxante") has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style. This action is a Jewish response to blasphemy (m. Sanhedrin 7.5; Jdt 14:16-17).
[翻訳注]  So BDAG 307 s.v. ἐκπηδάω 1, “rush (lit. ‘leap’) out…εἰς τὸν ὄχλον into the crowd Ac 14:14.”

[翻訳注]  Grk “shouting and saying.” The participle λέγοντες (legontes, in v. 15) has not been translated because it is redundant.[解説]  What follows is one of two speeches in Acts to a purely pagan audience ( in Athens is the other). So Paul focused on God as Creator, a common link.

15.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “with the same kinds of feelings,” L&N 25.32. BDAG 706 s.v. ὁμοιοπαθής translates the phrase “with the same nature τινί as someone.” In the immediate context, the contrast is between human and divine nature, and the point is that Paul and Barnabas are mere mortals, not gods.

[翻訳注]  Grk “in order that you should turn,” with ἐπιστρέφειν (epistrefein) as an infinitive of purpose, but this is somewhat awkward contemporary English. To translate the infinitive construction “proclaim the good news, that you should turn,” which is much smoother English, could give the impression that the infinitive clause is actually the content of the good news, which it is not. The somewhat less formal “to get you to turn” would work, but might convey to some readers manipulativeness on the part of the apostles. Thus “proclaim the good news, so that you should turn,” is used, to convey that the purpose of the proclamation of good news is the response by the hearers. The emphasis here is like 1 Thess 1:9-10.
[翻訳注]  Or “useless,” “futile.” The reference is to idols and idolatry, worshiping the creation over the Creator (Rom 1:18-32). See also 1 Kgs 16:2, 13, 26; 2 Kgs 17:15; Jer 2:5; 8:19; 3 Macc 6:11.

[翻訳注]  Grk “and the earth, and the sea,” but καί (kai) has not been translated before “the earth” and “the sea” since contemporary English normally uses a coordinating conjunction only between the last two elements in a series of three or more.

16.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “them, who in.” The relative pronoun (“who”) was replaced by the pronoun “he” (“In past generations he”) and a new sentence was begun in the translation at this point to improve the English style, due to the length of the sentence in Greek and the awkwardness of two relative clauses (“who made the heaven” and “who in past generations”) following one another.
[翻訳注]  On this term see BDAG 780 s.v. παροίχομαι. The word is a NT hapax legomenon.
[翻訳注]  Or “all the Gentiles” (in Greek the word for “nation” and “Gentile” is the same). The plural here alludes to the variety of false religions in the pagan world.

17.en: [翻訳注]  The participle ἀγαθουργῶν (agaqourgwn) is regarded as indicating means here, parallel to the following participles διδούς (didou") and ἐμπιπλῶν (empiplwn). This is the easiest way to understand the Greek structure. Semantically, the first participle is a general statement, followed by two participles giving specific examples of doing good.
[翻訳注]  Or “from the sky” (the same Greek word means both “heaven” and “sky”).

[翻訳注]  Grk “satisfying [filling] your hearts with food and joy.” This is an idiomatic expression; it strikes the English reader as strange to speak of “filling one’s heart with food.” Thus the additional direct object “you” has been supplied, separating the two expressions somewhat: “satisfying you with food and your hearts with joy.”

[解説]  God’s general sovereignty and gracious care in the creation are the way Paul introduces the theme of the goodness of God. He was trying to establish monotheism here. It is an OT theme (Gen 8:22; Ps 4:7; 145:15-16; 147:8-9; Isa 25:6; Jer 5:24) which also appears in the NT (Luke 12:22-34).

18.en: [翻訳注]  The participle λέγοντες (legontes) is regarded as indicating means.

[翻訳注]  BDAG 524 s.v. καταπαύω 2.b gives both “restrain” and “dissuade someone fr. someth.,” but “they scarcely dissuaded the crowds from offering sacrifice,” while accurate, is less common in contemporary English than saying “they scarcely persuaded the crowds not to offer sacrifice.” Paganism is portrayed as a powerful reality that is hard to reverse.

19.en: [解説]  Antioch was a city in Pisidia about 90 mi (145 km) west northwest of Lystra.[地図]  For location see JP1-E2; JP2-E2; JP3-E2; JP4-E2.
[解説]  Iconium was a city in Lycaonia about 18 mi (30 km) north of Lystra. Note how Jews from other cities were chasing Paul (2 Cor 11:4-6; Gal 2:4-5; Acts 9:16).
[翻訳注]  The participle πείσαντες (peisante") is taken temporally (BDAG 791 s.v. πείθω 1.c).
[翻訳注]  Grk “stoning Paul they dragged him.” The participle λιθάσαντες (liqasante") has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

20.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “and entered”; the word “back” is not in the Greek text but is implied.

[翻訳注]  Grk “And on.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
[解説]  Derbe was a city in Lycaonia about 35 mi (60 km) southeast of Lystra. This was the easternmost point of the journey.[地図]  For location see JP1-E2; JP2-E2; JP3-E2.

21.en: [解説]  Lystra was a city in Lycaonia about 35 mi (60 km) northwest of Derbe.[地図]  For location see JP1-E2; JP2-E2; JP3-E2.
[解説]  Iconium was a city in Lycaonia about 18 mi (30 km) north of Lystra.
[解説]  Antioch was a city in Pisidia about 90 mi (145 km) west northwest of Lystra.[地図]  For location see JP1-E2; JP2-E2; JP3-E2; JP4-E2.

22.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “to Antioch, strengthening.” Due to the length of the Greek sentence and the tendency of contemporary English to use shorter sentences, a new sentence was started here. This participle (ἐπιστηρίζοντες, episthrizonte") and the following one (παρακαλοῦντες, parakalounte") have been translated as finite verbs connected by the coordinating conjunction “and.”

[解説]  And encouraged them to continue. The exhortations are like those noted in Acts 11:23; 13:43. An example of such a speech is found in Acts 20:18-35. Christianity is now characterized as “the faith.”
[解説]  This reference to the kingdom of God clearly refers to its future arrival.

23.en: [翻訳注]  The preposition κατά (kata) is used here in a distributive sense; see BDAG 512 s.v. κατά B.1.d.

[翻訳注]  Literally with a finite verb (προσευξάμενοι, proseuxamenoi) rather than a noun, “praying with fasting,” but the combination “prayer and fasting” is so familiar in English that it is preferable to use it here.

[翻訳注]  BDAG 772 s.v. παρατίθημι 3.b has “entrust someone to the care or protection of someone” for this phrase. The reference to persecution or suffering in the context (v. 22) suggests “protection” is a better translation here. This looks at God’s ultimate care for the church.

24.en: [翻訳注]  Grk “Then passing through Pisidia they came.” The participle διελθόντες (dielqonte") has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
[解説]  Pamphylia was a province along the southern coast of Asia Minor.

25.en: [解説]  Perga was a city in Pamphylia near the southern coast of Asia Minor.
[解説]  Attalia was a seaport in the province of Pamphylia on the southern coast of Asia Minor, about 12 mi (20 km) southwest of Perga.

26.en: [解説]  Antioch was the city in Syria (not Antioch in Pisidia) from which Paul’s first missionary journey began (see Acts 13:1-4). That first missionary journey ends here, after covering some 1,400 mi (2,240 km).[地図]  For location see JP1-F2; JP2-F2; JP3-F2; JP4-F2.

[翻訳注]  Or “committed.” BDAG 762 s.v. παραδίδωμι 2 gives “commended to the grace of God for the work 14:26” as the meaning for this phrase, although “give over” and “commit” are listed as alternative meanings for this category.

[翻訳注]  BDAG 829 s.v. πληρόω 5 has “to bring to completion an activity in which one has been involved from its beginning, complete, finish” as meanings for this category. The ministry to which they were commissioned ends with a note of success.

27.en: [解説]  Note that God is the subject of the activity. The outcome of this mission is seen as a confirmation of the mission to the Gentiles.
[解説]  On the image of opening, or of the door, see 1 Cor 16:9; 2 Cor 2:12; Col 4:3.

28.en: [翻訳注]  BDAG 238 s.v. διατρίβω gives the meaning as “spend” when followed by an accusative τὸν χρόνον (ton cronon) which is the case here.
